headline_marked: [[Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir to be sworn in as 23rd President]] of Bangladesh today
headline: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir to be sworn in as 23rd President of Bangladesh today
summary: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir will take the oath as the 23rd President of Bangladesh today. The ceremony will be held at 7 PM at Bangabhaban's Darbar Hall, administered by the Acting Speaker.
details: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, the newly elected President of Bangladesh, will take his oath of office today. The state ceremony is scheduled for 7 PM on Friday, August 21, at the Darbar Hall of Bangabhaban.
The Acting Speaker of the Jatiya Sangsad, Barrister Kawsar Kamal, will administer the oath to the newly elected President.

High-profile guests including the outgoing President, Prime Minister, Speaker, Chief Justice, and cabinet members will be present. Chiefs of the three armed forces, foreign diplomats, and other distinguished personalities are also expected to attend.

The presidential election was held on Thursday, August 20, at the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban. BNP-nominated candidate Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir won by a large margin, securing 255 votes through the direct vote of Members of Parliament.

His sole opponent, Colonel (Retd.) Oli Ahmad of the LDP, received 88 votes. Chief Election Officer and CEC A. M. M. Nasir Uddin officially declared Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir as the winner after the vote count.
Subsequently, a government gazette confirming his election was issued, signed by Akhtar Ahmed, Senior Secretary of the Election Commission.

headline_marked: [[Imran Khan transferred to hospital]] from prison under strict security for health checks
headline: Imran Khan transferred to hospital from prison under strict security for health checks
summary: Pakistan's former Prime Minister Imran Khan was moved from prison to a hospital in Islamabad following a Supreme Court order for necessary health examinations. The transfer was conducted under heavy security.
details: Former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan has been transferred from prison to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad under strict security measures. This move follows a Supreme Court directive for him to undergo necessary health examinations.
The transfer took place late Thursday night, with Khan escorted by a robust police convoy. Authorities sealed off the entire area surrounding the hospital in advance to ensure maximum security.

Over 800 personnel from the police, prison authorities, paramilitary Pakistan Rangers, and local administration were deployed. Senior police officials had also inspected the hospital's overall security situation prior to his arrival.

The Supreme Court had issued an order on Tuesday, instructing Khan's transfer for health checks within 48 hours. The government's challenge to this directive was directly rejected by Pakistan's highest court.

The 73-year-old former prime minister has been imprisoned since August 2023. Concerns about his continuously deteriorating physical condition have been repeatedly raised by his party members and family over the past year.
Khan faces multiple charges, including cases related to state gifts (Toshakhana) and an illegal marriage. While some convictions have been overturned, several other cases remain pending against him.
